# What is Comp Bio?

---

***Computational biology***

-   The study of life using computational techniques, theoretical models, and
    data
-   Conceptual

. . .

***Bioinformatics***

-   Creating tools (algorithms, databases) to solve biological problems
-   More applied


## Comp Bio is as broad as biology

::: {.incremental}
-   All fields of biology can now generate enormous quantities of data that
    require computational approaches
-   For this class, we will focus on:
    -   Evolutionary biology
    -   Molecular evolution & phylogenetics
    -   Genomics
-   Modeling and computational skills generalize to other fields
:::

## Algos & models used in comp bio

A ***model*** is a parametric explanation of biological observations

. . .

An ***algorithm*** is a set of instructions for solving a problem

## Probabilistic models

-   Maximum likelihood
-   Bayesian inference
-   Machine learning
-   Markov chain models

Used across biology

## Algorithms

-   String algos
    -   sort, search, etc
-   Optimization algos
    -   Dynamic programming
    -   Linear programming
    -   Greedy algos, heuristic methods
    -   Expectation-maximization

Used across biology

## Science is based on models

>   All science is based on models, and every scientific model comprises three
>   distinct stages: statement of well-defined hypotheses; deduction of all the
>   consequences of these hypotheses, and nothing but these consequences;
>   confrontation of these consequences with observed data.
>   - Maurice Allais

. . .

>   All models are wrong, but some models are useful.
>   - George Box


# Course overview

## Course format

::: {.incremental}
-   This course will be in-person
-   We will do a mix of
    -   Lecture
    -   "Follow-along" demos
    -   Exercises
-   I will record classes as Panopto webcasts and post them to Canvas
    -   BUT, this will not replace exercises
:::

## Course objectives

Enable you to:

::: {.incremental}
-   Apply basic Linux/Unix command-line utilities
-   Use basic programming for data processing
-   Use version-control tools for reproducibility
-   Understand probabilistic models for biological questions
-   Encode and apply computational algorithms to biological data
:::

. . .

***Learn computational approaches to processing biological data and modeling
biological ideas***

# Assignments & Grading

## My philosophy for high-level courses

::: {.incremental}
-   I assume you're here for the right reasons
-   If so, I think you'll have fun and learn a lot
-   At your stage, you should be motivated to acquire knowledge and skills
    -   Not by grades
-   Can you get a good grade without learning much?
    -   Quite possibly
:::

## Lab exercises

::: {.incremental}
-   Low-stake opportunities to apply what you're learning
-   Mostly completed in class
-   Work together, but submit your own work
-   Graded for effort
-   We will do a number of these and your 2 lowest scores will be dropped
:::

## Capstone projects

::: {.incremental}
-   Similar in format to exercises, but more challenging
-   Do not work together
-   Graded for correctness
-   Mostly done out of class, but you will have opportunities to work on them
    in class
-   Start early and use office hours
:::

## Late exercises and projects

-   20% deduction per day late


## Course grading 

| Item | Grade % |
|---|---|
| Lab exercises | 60% |
| Capstone projects | 40% |

: Breakdown of grading component percentages {#tbl-points}

Your final percentage will be calculated as:

Final percent = ( lab exercises % $\times$ 0.6 )

$+$ ( capstone projects % $\times$ 0.4 )

## Grading scale

| Percentage | Grade |
|---|---|
|  $\geq$ 90% | A |
| 80.0 -- 90.0% | B |
| 70.0 -- 80.0% | C |
| 60.0 -- 70.0% | D |
| < 60.0% | F |
